answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Call the lantern the capital, the spiral the age bonus, and the dune the compounding curve: only undivided lantern keeps the spiral, and the dune shows exactly how much a split loses. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
